lead.headline: Mahomes Sold Saturday, The Owner Gone By Sunday, And The Man Who Replaced Him Has Been Away Three Years
lead.dek: Too High Safeties traded Patrick Mahomes for five picks at 5.54 on Saturday evening and had a different owner by Sunday afternoon. He is not a new one. The last time the Cartel saw Davis he had just won the closest game in league history and lost the next one by 2.36. He has made three trades since he sat down, and the manager on the other end of two of them handed over an identical bundle of picks for Patrick Mahomes and for Parker Washington inside forty hours.
body: THE CARTEL — The twelfth roster in this league changed hands between Saturday night and Sunday afternoon and nobody announced it. The transaction log did. crmcd94, 0-7 and last in the league on every measure it keeps, sent Patrick Mahomes to Not F*cking Around Crew at 5.54 on Saturday evening for five draft picks, and then he was gone. The roster is now owned by DavisNuaimi. It is 0-7, it has scored 600.14 points, and on Sunday it started two men who scored 0.00 — Gardner Minshew and Cade Otton — neither of whom was on a bye.

The trade first, because it is why the chair was empty. Mahomes went out for a 2027 first originally belonging to Cheddar Bobs, who are 6-1 and will therefore be handing over a pick from somewhere near the bottom of the round; 2027 seconds from Somewhat Goodfellas and Trade Calculator Guy; and two 2029 fourths the model prices below zero. He then scored 6.00 in his first Sunday for his new employer. Chasing Glory beat what was left of the roster that sold him by fifty points and change.

Now the part the league has spent two days on. Davis is not a new owner, he is a returning one, and his exit is on the record whether or not he would like it to be. In 2023 he ran a team called Let A Naysayer Know. In Week 14 he won 147.50 to 147.34, which is still the closest finish in the history of this competition and has survived three hundred and thirty-six games. The following week he lost a playoff game 144.64 to 142.28 — two points and thirty-six hundredths — to a manager then calling himself themichaelsmith, who is called barringinjury now and is sitting at 4-3. Davis lost a consolation game to the team now called COME AND TAKE IT and was not seen again for two full seasons and most of a third.

Where was Davis. Davis was not here for 2024, when Hoya Paranoia went 11-3 and won it. Davis was not here for 2025, when Chasing Glory went 12-2 and won it. He missed twenty-eight regular-season games, three rookie drafts and the entire arc of a man who went 0-14 in 2023 and turned himself into the owner of most of the 2027 first round. He also missed nothing at all happening to barringinjury, who has gone 19-9 across the two seasons Davis sat out, is 4-3 in this one, and has still never reached a final. Davis comes back with exactly as many Cartel championships as the man who sent him away.

Two more things he missed, both of them funny. In Week 6 of this season barringinjury lost a game by 2.36 points — the identical margin, to the hundredth, that he had used to end Davis's only year here. And on Sunday afternoon, while the twelfth roster was changing hands, the Crew got past Blame spanos by 1.16, the fifth-tightest result anybody here has ever posted. Davis still owns the first. The two games that bracket his entire Cartel career — the best finish in the record book and his own last stand — were settled by 2.52 points between them. He has been away three years and he is still the answer to the trivia question.

He has not eased in. Sunday afternoon, Tyler Allgeier went to Lovely Day for two 2029 thirds. Just before one on Monday morning he bought Bryce Young from Out. Of. Town. Shooters. for four picks including his own 2029 second, which looks strange until you remember that when Mahomes left on Saturday the starting quarterback of a superflex roster became Gardner Minshew. By 10.43 on Monday morning Parker Washington had gone to Not F*cking Around Crew. Three trades in forty-eight hours from a man whose last recorded act in this league was losing by two and a third points.

Which brings us to the one manager who has been here throughout, and to two invoices that do not match. This paper carries a valuation desk: every rostered player measured against what a free agent at his position returns each week in this league's scoring, aged on a curve fitted to real dynasty trades, with picks on the same scale. Saturday: Charles Robinson gives up a 2027 first and a pair of 2027 seconds and receives Mahomes. Both halves come out at 2.62 — a dead heat, honestly struck. Monday morning: he gives up a 2027 first and a pair of 2027 seconds again, and receives Parker Washington, who is worth 1.15. That gap is thirty-nine per cent. Fifteen is the limit past which this paper will not print even a trade it has invented.

So the ledger has shifted, and it has shifted away from the manager who assembled it. Seven of the twelve 2027 first-rounders belonged to the Crew on Friday. Five do now. Two of them sit on the 0-7 roster — the one Cheddar Bobs owe, and the Crew's own — beside ten 2027 selections in all, twenty-one across three drafts, and a three-hundred-dollar waiver balance nobody else comes close to. Not one player there is rated above replacement. Call it raw material rather than a rebuild, in the hands of somebody this league has not had to think about since 2023.

Briefly, the football, because it was ridiculous. Blame spanos got 96.9 per cent out of what he owned, left 4.30 on a bench that could not have helped him, and lost by 1.16. The Crew managed 74.5, abandoned 47.02 behind its starters, gave a receiver slot to Jalen Coker for 1.40 and a superflex slot to a quarterback worth 6.00, and won regardless. It now sits top of the dynasty board on 63.35 while the power rankings have it seventh. No other team is read so differently by the two. The simulation gives it 46.5 to be playing in January.

Correction. Two numbers in Tuesday morning's breaking column were taken off the wire before Monday night had been scored, and both were wrong. The Crew's win over Blame spanos was by 1.16, not by twenty-seven. Chasing Glory's win over Too High Safeties was by 50.10, not by twelve. Season totals had settled; individual box scores had not. This paper's own manual warns on precisely that point — that a week in progress looks finished. It was read first and ignored anyway.
This is a developing story.

notebook.title: Football Morning in the Cartel
intro: I have been doing this long enough to know that the week you remember is not usually the week that mattered, and this was both. A roster changed hands between Saturday night and Sunday lunchtime. Seven trades cleared inside six days. And the only game that will show up in the record book was decided by one point and sixteen hundredths, between two managers who had nothing to do with any of it.

Here is the part I keep turning over. Blame spanos filed 96.9 per cent of his roster’s ceiling. Four point three points on the bench, across thirty men. I have watched this league for four seasons and I can count the better lineup cards on one hand. He lost, and the manager who beat him left 47.02 points sitting there, which is more than some of these teams have scored at running back all year.
There is no lesson in that. There is just the scoreboard, which does not care how carefully you filled in the form.

ten_things: 1. The valuation desk prices Patrick Mahomes at 2.62 points per week above replacement. It prices the five picks Too High Safeties took for him at 2.62. I have been handed a lot of trade grades in my life and I have never seen one come out level to the cent, and I am not sure what to do with it except write it down.

2. The same desk prices what Charles Robinson gave up for Parker Washington on Monday — his own 2027 first, his own 2027 second, COME AND TAKE IT’s 2027 second — at 2.62 as well. Parker Washington is 1.15. Same outlay, forty hours apart, one of them fair and one of them 39 per cent the wrong way.

3. Cheddar Bobs bought a tight end. Hunter Henry, at one thirty-nine on Sunday afternoon, for a 2027 third and a 2028 fourth. This paper has been asking since Week 4 and I am obliged to record that he has done it. His tight ends have still scored 47.8 points all season, last in the league by a distance, and Henry’s 14.10 came with the lineup he had already filed.

4. Four of the seven trades this week involved Out. Of. Town. Shooters. He is 3-4 and 5.3 per cent to make the field, so selling is the correct instinct. He sold Rodgers, Stevenson, Aaron Jones and Brissett for four 2028 picks and the desk has the players at 4.38 and the picks at 1.29. That is a 55 per cent gap, the widest of the week in either direction.

5. barringinjury bought those four men at 8.45 on Sunday and had two of them in his lineup by one o’clock. Aaron Rodgers gave him 14.08. Aaron Jones gave him 3.10. He won by 63.88 anyway and is now 4-3, which in this league means almost nothing: the three teams on 4-3 are separated by twenty-four points of playoff probability.

6. Somebody should tell Raptor about Kirk Cousins. Two weeks running, Cousins has sat behind Tyler Higbee in a flex slot. Two weeks running, Chasing Glory has won anyway. The totals are 22.52 to 4.20 and 22.40 to 3.40. At some point a man gets rewarded for this and it stops being funny.

7. Lovely Day was 92.3 per cent efficient and lost by 63.88. Keith is 3-4 on an all-play record of 15-62, which means that if everybody played everybody every week he would be 15-62. I do not know how to say that more kindly and I work for him.

8. Too High Safeties started two men who scored 0.00 and neither was on a bye. Gardner Minshew at quarterback, Cade Otton in a flex. The lineup had been set before the roster changed hands, which is the only defence available and is a real one.

9. The dynasty board and the power rankings disagree about Not F*cking Around Crew by six places — first against seventh, the widest split in the league. They also disagree about COME AND TAKE IT by five, in the other direction: fourth in power, ninth on what he owns, and not one selection to his name in the next three rookie drafts.

10. Week 8 gives us Chasing Glory at Cheddar Bobs, 5-2 against 6-1, first and fifth in the power rankings, and the winner leads the West or the Central depending on which way it falls. It also gives us Somewhat Goodfellas against Too High Safeties, 1-6 against 0-7, which is the first game of the Davis era and the only one all season where neither team can finish above tenth.

intro: If you only looked at the scoreboard this week you would think the top of this league settled down. It did the opposite. Cheddar Bobs stayed first and everything underneath him reshuffled, because the third, fourth and fifth teams on this list are inside two hundredths of a ranking point of each other and the only thing splitting them is who happened to draw whom.

What I keep coming back to is how differently these rosters are built. Chasing Glory wins on running backs — 402.5 points, most in the league — and gets almost nothing from receiver. Somewhat Goodfellas is the exact mirror image and it has one win. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. leads the league at quarterback and is last at receiver, which is not a strategy, it is a roster that got sold in pieces.

And then there is the lineup card, which is the part nobody wants to talk about because it is the part that is entirely in your hands. Two teams at 4-3 filed 96.9 per cent and 74.5 per cent on Sunday. The one that filed 74.5 won. That will even out, and when it does, one of those two is going to be a lot further down this list.

rumors.title: Charles Robinson’s Notebook
rumors.byline: Charles Robinson · Not F*cking Around Crew, roster 11
rumors.standing: Standing disclaimer: none of this is reporting. Nobody quoted here has said a word to me, every trade below is invented, and I am in the standings — five of the twelve 2027 firsts are mine, and three of them were handed over by teams I write about below. Read accordingly.
lede: Four clubs are idle this weekend and the Cartel has read the schedule. Thirty-six men on active rosters are watching, and exactly two of them are filed in a starting lineup. Two out of thirty-six is a good number for a four-team bye, nobody should get a medal for it, and both exceptions happen to be sitting in the same fixture.

The other thing to notice is that nothing has happened. Not one claim, not one drop, not one cut, not one trade since the Week 7 scores were certified. Seven days ago this league ran seven trades inside six days and shifted twenty-three draft picks. Since Tuesday: nobody has touched anything. I would pump the brakes on reading intent into that. Most of it is simply that the managers with money cannot use it and the managers with a reason to spend are already out of the race.

What the bye week really did was audit the benches, and the audit turned up the same thing on three separate rosters. This is a superflex format. You file two quarterbacks and no more. A third one, however good, is a man you own and cannot play — and the desk keeps pricing him as an asset, because it prices what he would fetch rather than what he does for the ten names you hand in. Three teams at or above .500 are carrying one of those. Two of them have a hole he could fill.

Here is the part that matters. Of the seven teams at .500 or better, four have no waiver budget whatsoever, and one of those four owns no draft pick in any of the next three seasons. The phone list in this league has got very short, and a fair amount of why is me.

items.head: A 6-1 team is last at tight end and carrying a quarterback it cannot start
body: Cheddar Bobs sits 6-1, rated 32.6 per cent to lift the trophy, and has produced 47.8 points at tight end across seven weeks. The next-worst room in the Cartel is on 73.0. That is not a slump, it is an unfilled slot, and Sunday’s purchase of Hunter Henry was housekeeping rather than a repair.

He is also holding three quarterbacks the desk rates — Jared Goff at 3.17, Justin Herbert at 2.98, Matthew Stafford at 2.75 — and he files two of them, as everyone does. Herbert is the most valuable thing in this league that contributes nothing. On the table he is worth more than every tight end on every roster outside the top three. In a Cheddar Bobs lineup he is worth zero.

The man who ought to take that call is tdsmith23, and the shape of it is close to comic. The Shooters lead the Cartel in quarterback scoring on 327.76 points and no longer own a quarterback worth the word; they are also second in the league at tight end, with three of them filed this week because there is nothing else to file. Each has exactly the surplus the other needs, at the two positions nobody ever trades.

deal.label: The deal that makes sense
deal.verdict: 2.26 against 2.98, fourteen per cent toward the Shooters, which is the outer edge of what the desk will sign and not past it. Now the honest part: it buys Cheddar Bobs 0.46 points a week. That is the entire upgrade available to him, because there is no tight end for sale in this league, and a man with $150 and a 6-1 record deserves to be told that rather than sold a story. It moves the Shooters 2.46, which is more than anything else on their phone.

items.fit: Cheddar Bobs is twelfth of twelve at tight end and third at running back, with $150 and no 2027 first — that one is filed in Too High Safeties. The Shooters hold two 2027 seconds and three 2027 thirds and no first of any round, because theirs is mine, so a quarterback is something they can only buy with players, and the only players they have spare are tight ends.

items.head: I said somebody should ask Raptor about his spare quarterback. I checked. He has not got one
body: Last issue I wrote that Chasing Glory keeps leaving Kirk Cousins out and that it suggested more quarterback than he needs. That was lazy and the arithmetic says so. He files Brock Purdy and Dak Prescott in the two slots and Cousins is the third — which this week, with San Francisco idle, is the only reason he has a quarterback at all.

Run the sale through the desk and it comes back at under a point a week. Lift Prescott out of that lineup and the superflex drops to a receiver or a fourth back, and Chasing Glory has not got the receivers for it: first in the league at running back on 402.5 points, tenth at receiver on 211.2. The imbalance is real. The quarterback is not the lever.

What makes him genuinely stuck is the part that is my fault. He owns no 2027 pick in any round and nothing better than a third in 2028 or 2029. He is 89.4 per cent to win the Central and he cannot pay for a thing except out of a starting lineup that runs at 91.6 per cent, the most accurate in the league. There is no deal here. I wanted there to be one.
items.fit: Raptor’s best draft asset across three years is a 2028 third. His 2027 first belongs to Trade Calculator Guy. He has $0 of waiver budget. For a side two games clear in its division that is a closed shop, and I am one of the two people who closed it.

items.head: BADS is 5-2 with no picks, no money and one position to fix
body: COME AND TAKE IT owns nothing in 2027, nothing in 2028 and nothing in 2029. Not a fourth. He has no waiver budget either. At 5-2 the simulations make him 95.3 per cent a playoff team and 11.2 per cent a champion, and the market board has him twelfth of twelve at 92,007 — which is the price of having spent everything on a team that is actually good.

The hole is quarterback and it is the only one. He is second in the Cartel at running back on 390.0 points and tenth at quarterback on 203.72, in a format that starts two of them. There is one route out of that for a man with no currency, which is to pay in backs, and he has the depth to do it without touching the one he leans on.

At the other end, igross has every reason to sell an eight-point-a-week quarterback: 2-5, 0.6 per cent, and Jalen Hurts on injured reserve waiting to be the same player next September. What I’m told about deals shaped like this one is that the seller always wants the pick. He should want the back. Picks are what got him to 2-5.

deal.label: The deal I would actually make
deal.verdict: 3.43 against 3.24 — three per cent, the tightest thing in this column and the cleanest shape in the league. BADS puts 1.91 a week into his starting ten and igross takes 2.43 out of his, which is precisely what a 5-2 buyer and a 2-5 seller are each meant to do. It happens the moment igross stops insisting on paper and takes a twenty-six-year-old starter instead.

items.fit: BADS has $0 and nothing to select with for three drafts; his 2027 first is mine. Javonte Williams is his second back, and behind Kyren Williams he would still hold Chuba Hubbard, Rachaad White and Bhayshul Tuten. igross holds $199 and thirteen picks across three years, and has conceded 990.30 points, more than any other roster — a combination that only ever means one thing.

items.head: The tight end nobody should buy is the second-dearest one on the table
body: Harold Fannin is priced at 4.31. Only Trey McBride costs more at the position and nothing else is near — Brock Bowers is 3.85 and then it falls off a cliff. Fannin is producing 2.44 a week. Bowers is producing 5.98. The front page of this paper corrected a Fannin figure in Week 7 and the desk has not moved him since, which it will tell you itself: the table is a Week 4 snapshot.

So when somebody rings igross about a tight end this fortnight, and somebody will, the number quoted at them will be the 4.31 and the thing being sold will be the 2.44. I want to be careful here, because the player may well be worth it in two years and that is genuinely what the price is measuring. It is not what a 6-1 side buying for January is measuring.

This is the stretch of the market I would leave alone altogether. Ten of the twelve tight end rooms in this league sit between 73 and 155 points for the season. There is no edge in there to buy. Spend the money on a receiver or spend none of it.
items.fit: Across the twelve rosters, 23.1 per cent of all held value rests on men the Cartel has put in a lineup twice or less — the board’s own softest figure, and it comes out of the same table every deal here is priced from. Fannin is not one of those men; he has the starts. The argument against his price is not that it is unproven, it is that he has proved something smaller than the price.

items.head: I own the first pick in the 2027 draft, and I did not have to be good to get it
body: Too High Safeties is 95.5 per cent to finish twelfth. His own 2027 first has been mine since October 2024, bought off the manager who used to own that roster two years before he walked away from it. Put those two sentences together and I am holding what the simulations call a 95.5 per cent chance at the top selection of a four-round rookie draft, in a season where my own team is 4-3.

I have written round the edges of this for three weeks and never said it that plainly, which was cowardice. Five of the twelve 2027 firsts are mine. Four belong to teams whose playoff odds run from 0.6 per cent up to 95.3, and those four will land wherever the seasons land them. The fifth is an appointment.

The reverse side is also mine to own. My own first went to that same roster on Monday morning and Cheddar Bobs’ went on the Saturday, which leaves the 0-7 team holding two firsts belonging to sides currently 6-1 and 4-3. The read — and this is a read — is that he should sell both of them this fortnight, while four contenders still believe they are buying in January, rather than hold late picks he has no use for. Whether a man who has owned the roster less than a week is thinking that way, I have no idea.
items.fit: Twelve 2027 firsts exist. Mine are the ones belonging to BADS, the Shooters, Blame spanos, Trade Calculator Guy and Too High Safeties. Three teams at or above .500 hold no 2027 pick of any round at all: Chasing Glory, COME AND TAKE IT and Blame spanos. Nobody needs telling that those two sentences are the same sentence.

items.head: The worst-placed roster in the Cartel owns one back, and he is worth a first
body: Last week I said I would buy D’Andre Swift and pay a 2027 first for him. I would still do it, and I am no longer the natural buyer, because the man who needs him more is 70.1 per cent to qualify and I am 46.5.

Blame spanos has Bijan Robinson, who produces 14.52 a week on the desk’s table, second only to Jahmyr Gibbs. Behind him it thins out fast: Breece Hall was questionable last week, Zach Charbonnet was ruled out, and both are filed tonight. He also holds two 2029 firsts and no 2027 pick whatsoever, so he can pay for a back without touching anything he plays.

deucebrat is 0.2 per cent to reach the playoffs and last of twelve on held value at 17.29, and Swift at 2.41 is the most valuable man he owns. A 3-4 seller who keeps winning games he has not earned is the hardest kind to shift, and the luck figure of plus 1.64 is why — nothing in his record is telling him to sell. Everything else is.

deal.label: The deal that makes sense
deal.verdict: 2.41 against 2.09, seven per cent toward spanos and comfortably inside tolerance. It adds 4.00 a week to a contender’s starting ten — the largest single lineup swing available anywhere in this league tonight — and costs Lovely Day 4.95, which is what selling honestly looks like. I should disclose that I would rather it did not happen, since spanos is 70.1 per cent to be in the field, I am 46.5, and I own his 2027 first.

items.fit: spanos holds two 2029 firsts, two 2028 seconds and nothing in 2027. deucebrat holds six picks in all across three years and $80. Skattebo is twenty-four and priced at 1.13; the 2029 first carries 0.96 on the pick curve, which is most of the deal and the only part of it a side at 0.2 per cent should care about.

heard: Nobody in this league has made a transaction of any kind since Tuesday. No claim, no add, no cut, no trade. In a twelve-team league in the last week of October that is not calm, it is gridlock, and the shape of it is the money: the $905 still unspent sits with four managers who are 6-22 between them, while the four who have nothing left are 18-10.

Both bye-week starters are in the same fixture, which is worth a sentence. Somewhat Goodfellas has Malachi Fields filed against New York’s week off and genuinely has nothing better — his bench holds no priced man and the ten he handed in is already his optimum. Lovely Day has Kendre Miller filed against New Orleans’ week off and does have something better. There is a difference between a hole and a mistake, and it is worth about four points a week.

Somewhat Goodfellas is formally eliminated in Week 8 while holding the third most valuable roster on the market board and twenty-three draft picks across three years, and he has spent none of his $200 all season. I keep returning to that roster because it is the cleanest case in the league of a man whose work does not pay out until 2028, and there is no way to make it arrive sooner.

The four most valuable rosters on the market board are 14-14 between them. Hoya Paranoia is 5-2 of that, and he is also 61.0 per cent to take a first-round bye having lost four men to byes this weekend, which tells you how far clear the top of this league has pulled. The rest of us are first, third and fourth on a board and 9-12 on the field.

I would stop short of calling five 2027 firsts a strategy this season. A strategy would have a quarterback room better than seventh and a running back room better than ninth inside it. What I have is a bet on a draft I will be writing about rather than playing in, which is a thing you are allowed to do once.

draft_column.byline: Mel Kiper Jr. · the board, four drafts deep
intro: Five weeks of 2026 production are in the book and the board has moved, so let me bring you up to date. Four hundred and thirty-two selections across five drafts — 240 in the 2023 startup and 48 apiece in the 2023 rookie draft, 2024, 2025 and 2026 — and every one of them graded on what it has produced in a starting lineup. Not on what I said about it at the time. Not on what the trade calculator says about it this morning.

The order of my board is unchanged and every number underneath it is not. Each of the twelve managers gained between 2.1 and 6.0 points per selection this week, which is what five more weeks of football does to a denominator that has not moved. Chasing Glory stays first at 270.7 points a pick from TWENTY picks — twenty! — and the margin to second place has widened again: 55.8 this morning against 54.4 last week. Make a fifth as many selections as the man at the bottom of this page and average more than double his return, and that is not variance, that is a scout.

Here is the thing I want on the record this week. There are five selections in the history of this league that have produced a thousand points or more, and Sunday added the fifth. Four of the five are quarterbacks and the newest is not. Two of the five are still owned by the man who called the name and three of them are not, and the two that moved — Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes — were the first and second overall selections of the startup. In a superflex league where sixty-seven quarterbacks are rostered for twenty-four weekly slots, that is the whole market in four sentences.

1.note: Twenty selections, eight hits, 270.7 a pick — the best figure on my board by 55.8, and the margin grew again this week. Jahmyr Gibbs at 1.05 of the 2023 rookie draft added 39.20 on Sunday and crossed a thousand points: 1,006.30, fifth-most productive selection this league has ever made and the only member of that group still playing for the manager who drafted him. Jordan Love in the seventh round of the startup, 857.28, and Love has been somebody else's quarterback for a while now. Three of the twenty are still on this roster, which tells you he treats a pick as currency rather than a keepsake. The drafting is elite and the conversion is better.

10.note: Thirty-four selections, fourteen hits, fourteen retained, 214.9 a pick — second on my board and the only manager who manages volume, hit rate and retention all at once. Lamar Jackson at 1.10 of the startup for 1,063.14 is third all-time in this league and he still owns him, which in this format is rarer than the pick itself. C.J. Stroud at 1.04 in the 2023 rookie draft. George Kittle in the EIGHTH round of the startup for 606.00 is the most productive tight end anybody in this league has ever selected and Kittle plays for 100 Yards And Runnin now. The blemish stays Travis Hunter at 1.03 in 2025 on zero, and Sleeper files him at defensive back, which makes it construction rather than evaluation.

6.note: Twenty-five picks, nine hits, 205.6 a selection, third on my board. Josh Allen at 1.02 of the 2023 startup has produced 1,333.70 points, the most productive selection in the history of this league by 219.28 — and Josh Allen plays for 100 Yards And Runnin, while this roster sits eleventh in the league in quarterback production. That is the review in one sentence and it has been for three years. Now the part that is genuinely outstanding: Jeremiyah Love at 1.01 and Carnell Tate at 1.02 in 2026, 47.60 and 38.90, the two most productive picks of a forty-eight-man class, both 21 years old and both still here. Five of twenty-five retained overall. He finds them and he sells them.

7.note: Twenty-six selections, twelve hits, 199.0 a pick, fourth on my board. Joe Burrow at 1.03 of the startup for 727.14 is the anchor and he kept him. Bijan Robinson, who has delivered 93.70 points above replacement in five starts since arriving, was drafted 1.01 of the 2023 rookie draft by Somewhat Goodfellas — the best player on this roster came out of somebody else's board. Four of twenty-six still here, third-lowest retention in the league. And across twenty-six selections I cannot find a tight end worth discussing, which is precisely the slot now costing him a first-round bye.

8.note: Thirty-four picks, ten hits, 196.0 a selection, and that average is carried by two extraordinary swings rather than by breadth. Jalen Hurts at 1.04 of the startup for 1,114.42, second all-time in this league, and he still has him. Baker Mayfield in the TWELFTH round for 888.56 — more than four times what that round returns and the finest value selection this league has produced — and Mayfield now sits behind four other quarterbacks on COME AND TAKE IT's roster. Travis Kelce at 2.17 of the startup for 484.00 is still here too. Twelve of thirty-four retained. Kaleb Johnson at 1.09 in 2025 remains on zero.

11.note: Forty-eight selections, second-most in this league, twenty-four hits — three more than anybody — sixteen retained, 195.3 a pick. The volume is the identity and this week the top end finally spoke: Drake Maye, taken 1.06 in 2024, posted 45.46 on Sunday, the largest individual score anybody has managed in the Cartel this season, and sits on 622.30 for his career. Ashton Jeanty at 1.01 in 2025 is on 249.80 and is the single most valuable asset in this league on the valuation desk's numbers, and he has not been in a lineup for two weeks. Kenyon Sadiq at 1.08 in 2026 is on zero. Seven of the twelve 2027 firsts are in this drawer, so the board is about to double, and volume is already what he has most of.

2.note: Thirty picks, eleven hits, 173.8 a selection — and two still on the roster. TWO! Patrick Mahomes at 1.01 of the startup for 1,009.50, fourth all-time, and Mahomes is sitting on an 0-5 roster the model gives a 0.0% chance of January. De'Von Achane at 1.12 of the 2023 rookie draft, now on Not F*cking Around Crew's injured reserve. He evaluates adequately and he trades everything, and he owns no selection before a 2029 second, which means this board stops growing until the end of the decade.

3.note: Fifty-three picks, twenty-one hits, 167.5 a selection. Volume without return, and the recent classes are the reason: Jordyn Tyson at 1.03 and Makai Lemon at 1.05 in 2026 are both on zero and KC Concepcion at 1.07 is on 2.90. Bryce Young at 1.02 of the 2023 rookie draft for 559.36 is the hit — he traded Young, bought him back, and started Jacoby Brissett ahead of him on Sunday. Trey McBride in the TWELFTH round of the startup for 605.70 is the second-best tight end selection in league history and McBride plays for Hoya Paranoia. Ten of fifty-three retained, and no 2027 pick in any round, so the volume stops here as well.

5.note: Thirty-eight selections, twelve hits, 155.8 a pick, and EIGHTEEN still on the roster — the highest retention figure in this league by two, which tells you he believes his own evaluations more than anybody. Bijan Robinson at 1.01 of the 2023 rookie draft for 981.30 and Jaxon Smith-Njigba at 1.06 for 743.76 are both first-rate calls; he traded the first and kept the second, and Smith-Njigba gave him 22.30 on Sunday. Against that: Fernando Mendoza at 1.04, Eli Stowers at 1.10 and Omar Cooper at 1.11 in 2026 are all on zero — three first-rounders, one class, one manager, nothing. Four 2028 firsts are still to come.

4.note: Fifty-six selections, more than anybody in this league, seventeen hits, 155.3 a pick, tenth on my board. Volume has not been kind to him. Marvin Harrison at 1.01 of 2024 is on Not F*cking Around Crew now and has not started a game there; Ty Simpson at 1.09 in 2026 is on zero; twelve of fifty-six are retained. What lifts the grade off the floor is the one room nobody else in this league drafts: Brock Bowers at 1.08 in 2024 for 453.10, still here, 25.00 on Sunday, and the best tight end production in the Cartel at 147.00 — he drafted one half of that room and acquired the other. He also made the pick that produced Sam LaPorta, 2.19 in the 2023 rookie draft, 466.30, who plays for somebody else.

9.note: Twenty-nine picks, nine hits, 150.7 a selection, eleven retained — and he is 5-0, which makes this the weakest board belonging to any contender and a real finding rather than a quibble. Zay Flowers at 1.09 of the 2023 rookie draft has returned 557.00 and is still here; Quentin Johnston at 1.07 of the same draft has returned 102.00. Those are the two ends of one evening's work. He holds four 2027 selections and not one of them is a first or a second, because Not F*cking Around Crew has both. A 5-0 roster assembled almost entirely through trade is a perfectly legitimate way to build in this format. It simply does not grade on my board.

12.note: Thirty-nine picks, eleven hits, 128.3 a selection — last on my board by 22.4 — and thirteen retained. The case for optimism is narrow and genuine: three of the five most productive selections of the 2026 class are his. Denzel Boston at 1.12 on 30.10, Jonah Coleman at 2.13 on 13.30, Jadarian Price at 1.06 on 12.00 — 55.40 points, 36.7% of everything forty-eight picks have produced league-wide. He holds seven 2027 selections and not a first, because that one belongs to Not F*cking Around Crew, and at 0-5 with a 91.9% chance of finishing last it is about to be the most valuable pick in the draft.

board.head: Jahmyr Gibbs is the fifth selection in league history to clear a thousand points, and the first who isn't a quarterback
board.body: 39.20 on Sunday took him to 1,006.30. The group above him: Josh Allen 1,333.70 at 1.02 of the startup, Jalen Hurts 1,114.42 at 1.04, Lamar Jackson 1,063.14 at 1.10, Patrick Mahomes 1,009.50 at 1.01. Three of those four went in the first five picks of the 2023 startup and two of the four have changed hands since — Allen, drafted by Lovely Day and now carrying 100 Yards And Runnin's superflex, and Mahomes, drafted by COME AND TAKE IT and now sitting on an 0-5 roster. Gibbs went 1.05 of the 2023 rookie draft to Chasing Glory and is the only man in the five playing for the manager who picked him.

board.head: Forty-eight picks, 151.0 points, and 141.9 of them belong to two managers
board.body: Jeremiyah Love at 1.01 on 47.60 and Carnell Tate at 1.02 on 38.90 are Lovely Day's. Denzel Boston at 1.12 on 30.10, Jonah Coleman at 2.13 on 13.30 and Jadarian Price at 1.06 on 12.00 are Too High Safeties'. That is 94.0% of a whole rookie class sitting on two rosters the model prices at 0.2% and 0.0%, and the other ten managers have managed 9.10 points from the thirty-seven picks they made between them, of which Antonio Williams, taken 2.14 by 100 Yards And Runnin, accounts for 3.60. Every year in this league the class lands on the teams who needed it least and every year it is treated as bad luck rather than as the draft order working exactly as designed.

board.head: Nine first-rounders are still on nothing, and the 2026 class owns seven of them
board.body: Two are hangovers from 2025: Travis Hunter, taken third overall, whom Sleeper files at defensive back and who therefore cannot score a point in this format, and Kaleb Johnson, ninth overall, who simply has not. The remaining seven are all 2026 — Tyson third, Mendoza fourth, Lemon fifth, Sadiq eighth, Simpson ninth, Stowers tenth, Cooper eleventh. Three of them were Somewhat Goodfellas' calls and two were Out. Of. Town. Shooters'. Seven blanks out of a twelve-man first round in the second week of October is perfectly normal and nobody should be alarmed by it. Seven blanks next October would mean the class never happened.

board.head: The two best tight end selections in league history went in the eighth and twelfth rounds, and neither man kept his
board.body: George Kittle, round 8 of the 2023 startup to Hoya Paranoia, 606.00 points — the most productive tight end anybody in this league has ever drafted. Trey McBride, round 12 of the same draft to Out. Of. Town. Shooters., 605.70. Kittle now plays for 100 Yards And Runnin and McBride for Hoya Paranoia, which is to say the man who found him sold him and then bought the other one. Travis Kelce went 2.17 for 484.00 and sits at 37 on a 1-4 roster. The one top-end tight end in this league still owned by the manager who drafted him is Brock Bowers, 1.08 in 2024. Four hundred and thirty-two selections and that is the list, in a format that pays a premium at the position and in which the two worst rooms belong to teams at 99.8% and 80.4% to make the playoffs.

board.head: The fifth round of the startup still beats the fourth, and the twelfth beats the eleventh by a hundred and twenty-two
board.body: The 2023 startup returns 835.6 a pick in the first round, 617.8 in the second, 491.0 in the third, and then it stops behaving like a draft. The fourth round averages 374.0 and the fifth 411.4. The eighth comes in at 370.1, which is the fourth round again, and the eighteenth at 172.6, which beats the eleventh, the thirteenth and every round that follows it. The eleventh collapses to 81.1 and the twelfth recovers to 203.2, and the reason is two names: Baker Mayfield went to Trade Calculator Guy in that round and Trey McBride went to Out. Of. Town. Shooters. in it. No line can be drawn through any of that. The useful reading is narrower: after the eighth round of a twenty-round startup there is no curve at all, only a scatter with a few live pockets in it, and the two men who reached into those pockets sit fifth and eighth on this page, which is a lesson of its own.

Mahomes has started 33 games for Too High Safeties and scored 634.4. The receiving team in this deal is 9-33 lifetime, which tells you how little one great trade fixes.

igross sold Saquon Barkley for Terry McLaurin and Zamir White. Barkley has started 33 games for Hoya Paranoia and produced 597.1 on the way to two titles. McLaurin gave Trade Calculator Guy 261.9 and White gave him 7.0 in two starts. This is how a dynasty gets built and how one doesn't.

Trevor Lawrence for Javonte Williams, Dorian Thompson-Robinson and a 2024 first. Lawrence started 21 games for Blame spanos and scored 439.7. Williams started two and produced 17.1 before being moved. The first-round pick was real value, but in superflex a starting quarterback at that price is a bargain that does not come around often.

Three running backs and a 2026 third for Josh Jacobs. Zack Moss, Rasheen Ali and Audric Estime combined for four points and one start between them. Jacobs has started 25 games for 100 Yards And Runnin and produced 439.1, and is still on the roster. This is the single most lopsided in-season trade in the record.

DK Metcalf and a 2025 first for Garrett Wilson, made on startup night. Metcalf started 31 games for Blame spanos and scored 366.5. Wilson started four for the other side, produced 36.6 and was traded on. The pick going back made this defensible at the time; the production has not been close since.

Sam LaPorta for Pat Freiermuth and two second-round picks. LaPorta has started 29 games for Not F*cking Around Crew and scored 317.7 and is still on the roster — one of the few long-term wins on a 13-29 résumé. Freiermuth never started a game for the team that acquired him.

Alvin Kamara and Amari Cooper for Cam Akers, Javonte Williams and two picks. Kamara alone has produced 496.8 across 34 starts for Cheddar Bobs. Akers started once. The picks softened it, but this is the trade that built the roster that went to the 2023 final.

George Kittle and two picks for Trey McBride. Kittle never started a game for Out. Of. Town. Shooters. McBride started 17 for Hoya Paranoia and produced 332.9, and went for 24.5 in the 205-point opener this season. Tight end premium scoring makes this position expensive and this deal is why.

Lovely Day's best trade, and it cost him Raheem Mostert, who never started a game for the team that took him. Tucker Kraft has started 17 games for Lovely Day, produced 191.6, and was in the lineup for 9.5 in the Week 1 win this season. Small trades decide more seasons than big ones.

Jonathan Mingo for De'Von Achane, made on startup night. Achane produced 121.9 in eight starts. Mingo never started a game. Mingo was also Lovely Day's own 1.11 pick in that same draft, which makes this one of the more instructive nights in league history.

Travis Kelce, Calvin Ridley and Josh Jacobs for David Njoku, Anthony Richardson and Zach Charbonnet, in the first week of the league's existence. The Kelce-and-Jacobs side produced 485.9; the other produced 201.8. It is the trade that made the 2023 season and the owner who won it is no longer in the league.

The most evenly matched trade in the record book. Garrett Wilson, Isaiah Likely and Jimmy Garoppolo for Brock Purdy and Sam Darnold: 446.0 against 469.4, a difference of 23 points across three seasons. Wilson started 33 games for Chasing Glory. Purdy started 17 on the other side. Nobody lost this and nobody has stopped arguing about it.

Travis Kelce, Calvin Ridley and Tony Pollard for Alec Pierce and Rashee Rice, at the 2024 deadline. Trade Calculator Guy got 326.5 out of it and a run to the final. Blame spanos got 159.7, mostly from Rice, and Pierce started once.

Daniel Jones for Tua Tagovailoa, which reads like a coin flip and was not. Jones produced 309.3 in 18 starts for COME AND TAKE IT; Tagovailoa gave Blame spanos 147.3 in ten. In superflex the second quarterback slot decides more weeks than anybody admits.

Deebo Samuel for Romeo Doubs and Khalil Shakir. Samuel started 26 games for Hoya Paranoia and produced 263.4 on a championship roster. Doubs and Shakir combined for 83.1 and eight starts. Hoya Paranoia's record in this column is starting to look less like luck.

initial.verdict: COME AND TAKE IT sent Kaelon Black, his own 2029 first and $40 for Chuba Hubbard on Friday evening and was rewarded inside 48 hours: Hubbard scored 27.40 from a flex in a 179.84-point week, the highest total of Week 4, and the playoff odds moved 53.2% to 84.0%, the largest single-week swing of the season. The production ledger on this deal reads 0.00 for both sides because the grading window does not open until the week after a trade, so the Hubbard number above is a box score and not yet a grade. On the logic: a 2-2 team with no draft capital left and the league's best running back room at 235.50 points bought the player who makes Sunday better with currency it had already decided not to use. That is coherent. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. takes a 24-year-old back, a first three off-seasons out and $40 that lifts him to the second-largest budget in the league, while sitting 3-1 with the worst receiver production in it at 76.40 — which makes the cash the most useful thing he received and the one he has yet to spend. The risk on A is a 27-year-old back in a dynasty league; the risk on B is that a 2029 first from a team this committed to winning now is worth less than it looks.

Chasing Glory paid his own 2029 first for Jordan Addison, a 24-year-old receiver, and started him immediately for 7.10 in a 144.02-point defeat. Production is held at 0.00 on both sides at this stage by design. The diagnosis behind it is sound and the circumstances made it close to forced: Chasing Glory is tenth in the league at receiver with 117.90 points, is the most efficiently managed roster in the league at 94.5% with only 34.88 points left on his bench in four weeks, and holds $24 of waiver budget — the lowest in the league — so a trade was the only lever he had. Paying a first that will not be exercised until 2029 for a player who helps in 2026 is the correct shape of deal for a team 74.0% to win its division. Somewhat Goodfellas, at 1-3 and 0.6%, sells a receiver from a group that leads the league at 238.76 points and adds a first to a collection that already holds four 2028 firsts and his own 2027. He is also last in the league at running back with 23.00 points, and nothing in this trade addresses that. Both sides did what their position in the table told them to do, which is why neither grade is higher.

Lovely Day sent Drew Lock, a 2028 third and a 2028 fourth to 100 Yards And Runnin for MarShawn Lloyd and Case Keenum. Production is 0.00 on both sides at this gate. The difficulty is not the price, it is the direction. Lovely Day was already last in the league in quarterback production at 74.66 points from a three-man room in a superflex format, with Jayden Daniels on injured reserve, and he responded by trading one of the three quarterbacks for a 38-year-old — claimed off waivers by the other side the week before — and a tenth running back for a roster that already ranked sixth at the position with ten of them. On Sunday he started RJ Harvey, a running back, in the superflex slot for the second week running, and the Week 5 lineup filed on Tuesday does it again. The structural hole is the same size and two 2028 picks have left the building. 100 Yards And Runnin adds a fourth quarterback behind Josh Allen and Sam Darnold for nothing he was using, picks up two picks, and keeps a tight end room that leads the league — a straightforward profit for a 2-2 team with the worst luck in the league. The B+ is for the price, not the ambition.

Both managers did the thing their record told them to do, which is rarer than it sounds.

Jameis Winston to Out. Of. Town. Shooters. for the Crew’s 2029 third. A marginal quarterback moving to the roster already ranked first at the position, paid for with a pick three years out. Neither side gave up anything that will decide a season, which is also the reason it is hard to call it a good use of a Thursday.

Deshaun Watson to Chasing Glory for Raptor’s own 2029 second, with a 2028 fourth going back. Raptor buys depth behind Brock Purdy at the cost of a pick he will not miss until the roster he is building now is old. eloper adds to a stockpile that is already the largest in the league and does not address a single thing wrong with his lineup.

Hoya Paranoia sends Xavier Worthy, Brian Thomas, Harold Fannin and its 2027 first for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jake Ferguson. jlundblad buys the best receiver in the deal and the tight end depth he wanted, and pays with three young players and a first. At 4-2 with the second-most valuable roster that is a defensible push, but he left 31.30 points on his bench two days later, which is the awkward part: this roster’s problem was never the talent.

Patrick Mahomes for Cheddar Bobs’ 2027 first, two 2027 seconds and two 2029 fourths. The valuation desk prices the player at 2.62 points per week above replacement and the five picks at 2.62, which is as close to a market-rate trade as this league has produced. The Crew gets the better quarterback in a format that starts two; Too High Safeties gets the first-round pick of a 6-1 team and two seconds from teams that are 1-6 and 2-5, which are the two best seconds in that round. Nobody won on price. Day one return was 6.00 with Michael Penix on 23.42 behind him, which is a lineup problem and not a trade problem.

Aaron Rodgers, Rhamondre Stevenson, Aaron Jones and Jacoby Brissett to 100 Yards And Runnin for four 2028 picks. The desk has the players at 4.38 and the picks at 1.29 — a 55 per cent gap, the widest of a very busy week. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. is 3-4 at 5.3 per cent and is right to be selling; he sold the four men four hours before kickoff and then filed the worst lineup anybody has filed in this league this season off what was left. barringinjury started two of the four immediately and won by 63.88. The direction of travel is correct for both teams and the price is not.

Tyler Allgeier to Lovely Day for COME AND TAKE IT’s 2029 third and Lovely Day’s own 2029 third. Allgeier does not appear on the valuation desk’s priced list at all, which means the model has him at or below replacement; the two picks are worth 0.18 between them. Paying a rounding error for a player priced at nothing is not a disaster, but Lovely Day is twelfth on the dynasty board and 0.2 per cent to make the playoffs, so the direction is wrong on principle. He scored 6.40 in Week 7 — for the team that sold him, under the platform’s lineup lock.

Hunter Henry and a 2029 fourth to Cheddar Bobs for COME AND TAKE IT’s 2027 third and a 2028 fourth. The desk has Henry at 0.97 and the picks going back at 0.17. This paper has been asking Cheddar Bobs to buy a tight end since Week 4, and he has bought one for almost nothing, which is the right way to answer the question. It does not close it: his tight ends have scored 47.8 points in seven weeks, last in the league, and Henry’s 14.10 on Sunday was filed in somebody else’s lineup.

Bryce Young to Too High Safeties for its own 2029 second, the Shooters’ 2027 third returning and the 2027 seconds of 100 Yards And Runnin and Lovely Day. The desk prices Young at 2.26 and the four picks at 1.42, a 23 per cent gap toward the buyer. The context is the part that justifies it: with Mahomes sold on Saturday the roster’s starting quarterback was Gardner Minshew, who scored 0.00 the next afternoon. You can argue about whether Bryce Young is the answer. There was undeniably a question.

Parker Washington to Not F*cking Around Crew for the Crew’s own 2027 first, its own 2027 second and COME AND TAKE IT’s 2027 second. The desk prices Washington at 1.15 and the three picks at 2.62 — 39 per cent lopsided, past the point where this paper will print a proposed trade as a sensible one. It is the same 2.62 the Crew paid for Mahomes forty hours earlier. Washington scored 0.00 in Week 7 and is not in the Week 8 lineup. The Crew is first on the dynasty board and this is how a lead gets spent.

Jaylen Waddle to Hoya Paranoia for Caleb Douglas and Mac Jones. The desk has Waddle at 0.99 against 0.90 for the pair, which is about as level as a two-for-one gets. Hoya Paranoia wanted a starter and started him for 6.80; the Shooters wanted a 23-year-old receiver and got one who put up 20.00 on their bench the same afternoon. Both teams did what their records say they should.

dynasty_column.byline: By Roy Cowgirl · A current NFL broadcaster · Name withheld at the writer's request
intro: The board moved this week and it moved in the direction nobody wanted. Not F*cking Around Crew is still first. It is first with less than it had on Friday.

Here is the arithmetic. He held seven of the twelve 2027 first-rounders. He holds five. His pick column went from 19.47 to 14.24 and his total from 67.43 to 63.35. He is still first by fourteen points. That is how far ahead he was and how much of a lead you can spend before anybody notices.

What he bought with it is one quarterback priced at fair value and one receiver priced at a premium. The quarterback scored 6.00. I am not going to pretend that is a judgement on the trade after one Sunday. It is a judgement on the lineup card.

Second is Hoya Paranoia and I want to say something plain about this roster. Forty-one point five per cent of what it owns is startable right now, the highest figure on the board. Second in power, second here. There is no gap to exploit and no story to tell. It is just a good team that is also well placed, which is the hardest thing on this list to build.

Now the divergences, because that is what this table is for. COME AND TAKE IT is fourth in the power rankings and ninth here. It holds no selection at all in the next three rookie drafts and it is 5-2. That team is renting. Trade Calculator Guy is ninth in power and fifth here, and none of what it owns clears replacement level on rate. Zero per cent startable. Both of those numbers are correct and they mean opposite things.

The bottom three changed order. Too High Safeties came up to tenth on the back of the picks it took for Mahomes — 6.17 of 2027 capital, second only to the Crew. Out. Of. Town. Shooters. is eleventh after selling four starters for 2028 paper. Lovely Day is twelfth, and it got there by buying a running back the model does not price at all.

Four rosters show nought per cent startable. Trade Calculator Guy, Lovely Day, Too High Safeties and Out. Of. Town. Shooters. That is not a bug and I checked it before I said it. It means nothing on those four rosters is currently producing above what this league can get off the wire at the same position, which is a sentence about rate, not about talent.
And now the part I have to say about my own table, because the lead column on this paper’s front page corrected two of its own figures this week and I am not going to sit above that.

Twenty-three point one per cent of all board value in this league rests on players this league has started twice or fewer. On three rosters it is worse than a third: Somewhat Goodfellas at 53.5 per cent, Out. Of. Town. Shooters. at 45.2, Too High Safeties at 36.0. Somewhat Goodfellas is eighth on this board and more than half of the reason is players nobody here has seen play. Read that row as a guess, because it is one.

The prices themselves are from Week 4 and have not been rebuilt in three weeks. Mahomes is priced as a Too High Safeties player on the underlying table. Allgeier is not priced at all. The board reassembles the rosters correctly but it values them on a three-week-old sheet, and a board that leans on stale prices should say so on its face rather than wait to be caught.
